articleTitle: Complex permittivity and anisotropy measurement of 3D-printed PLA at microwaves and millimeter-waves
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The use of 3D-printing based on extrusion depositing technologies for electromagnetic applications (such as dielectric antenna design or human mimicking tissues) is increasing as a low cost alternative to other small-scale fabrication technologies. As a result, it is of utmost scientific interest to know the exact dielectric properties of commercially available printable materials, such as polylactide acid (PLA). The extrusion depositing process may originate an anisotropic behavior of the material permittivity especially at mm-waves. We investigate this plastic's complex permittivity across the microwave spectrum from 0.5 GHz to 20 GHz and at 40 GHz and 60 GHz. We propose a new indirect method for the complex permittivity determination at microwave frequencies based on a microstrip line with stubs and a superstrate. At 40 GHz and 60 GHz, the printed PLA samples are characterized using waveguide and open resonator methods. Results show that throughout the tested frequency range the dielectric constant along the normal direction to the printing surface is around 2.75±0.05 and tan δ = (1.1±0.2)×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. However, at least for the tested mm-wave bands, the dielectric constant along the parallel direction to the printing surface is around 2.96, corresponding to nearly 7% anisotropy.

articleTitle: Setting and physical rationale of heterogeneous turning scatterer system mesh optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Simulation process of electromagnetic waves diffraction formulated in terms of MoM solution obtaining, as the first step of general meshing algorithm. As a scattering surface perfect conductor cylinder served. The task is complicated by the existence of a special inhomogeneity on the scattering surface, the presence of which must be well established as the result of scattering pattern analysis. Inhomogeneity is defined by the limiting case - through hole. Simulation describes the dynamic system wherein heterogeneity rotated relative to the cylinder axis. Physical origins of optimization parameters - morphology dependent resonances (MDR) provisions, within which special tunning cycle realized. Method of dynamic simulation - stepping movement of the object. The proposed algorithm has been tested in CAD, optimization results provide a significant gain in the specified accuracy, corresponding to standard CAD meshing rules.

articleTitle: Analysis of radio wave propagation at millimeter-wave band in tunnels for 5G communications
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation and measurement results at millimeter-wave frequency inside three different tunnels are presented. Through the simulation results the impacts of tunnel cross sectional shape and dimension on path loss and delay spread are analyzed. In addition, the antenna radiation pattern, its orientation and wall roughness in small railway tunnel are studied. The results are validated using preliminary measurement carried out in old railway tunnel.

articleTitle: Reconstructing complex permittivity of local inhomogeneites in a radio-transparent dielectric matrix located in a waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The results are presented of the numerical solution to the forward problem of the electromagnetic wave scattering by inhomogeneous dielectric bodies in a waveguide and inverse problem of determining parameters of dielectric inclusions from the values of the transmission coefficient of the scattered electromagnetic wave. A comparison with the results of mesurements and analysis of the achieved threshold computational accuracy levels enable one to estimate and validate the simulation results and formulate the ways of improving the model and codes.

articleTitle: Detection of regions of interest in retinal images using artificial neural networks and K-means clustering
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The paper presents a new method for detecting and localizing regions of interest (ROI) in retinal images. In the learning phase, the focus is on an efficient feature selection based on K-means clustering of feature values and on artificial neural networks (ANNs) for image processing and textural features computation. Finally, a voting scheme identifies the regions of interest. The experiments were conducted to detect the optic disc, macula, exudates and hemorrhages. The results obtained on 150 test images show the efficiency of the proposed method in terms of accuracy, compared with other similar researches.

articleTitle: High-resolution optical vector network analyzer based on silicon-on-insulator coupled-resonator optical waveguides
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: A high-resolution optical vector network analyzer (OVNA) based on integrated silicon-on-insulator multi-microring coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The key functionality of the CROW filter is to perform wideband optical single sideband suppression for the implementation of an OVNA, which has been experimentally verified. The magnitude and phase response measurements of the stimulated Brillouin scattering in a single-mode fibre and a highly nonlinear fibre are successfully demonstrated. A high measurement resolution of 23.4 kHz is achieved.

articleTitle: An Aeronautical Ad Hoc Network routing protocol based on air vehicles movement features
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: To solve the problem that the current routing protocols in MANET cannot be used in AANET (Aeronautical Ad Hoc Networks), we propose the Hierarchical Space routing protocol (HSRP). Section 1 of the full paper gives five definitions that we have come up to find useful in describing HSRP protocol. Section 2 uses the above-mentioned five definitions to design the HSRP protocol; the HSRP protocol has the ability to dynamically change the update frequency of HELLO beacon and adjust the radius of routing space in according with the air traffic; section 2 also gives the architecture of HSRP protocol and the procedure for implementing the HSRP algorithm. Section 3 does three experiments to test the HSRP protocol. The experimental results, shown in Fig.1, Fig.2 and Fig.3 of section 2, indicate preliminarily that the HSRP protocol compared with ZRP protocol can adapt better to the impact of air vehicles density change on routing protocol and has higher delivery ratio, lower routing control overhead and lower average end-to-end delay, in addition, the HSRP is practical and effective in AANET.

articleTitle: BER for higher order laser modes in optical wireless underwater communications
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Average bit error rate (<;BER>) of an underwater optical communication system is analyzed for higher order laser beams. For this purpose, the effects of oceanic turbulence parameters and link parameters on single mode higher order laser beams are investigated.

articleTitle: Combined system of the microstrip antennas with different frequencies
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The combined system with microstrip antennas (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>=1.85GHz; f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>=3.7GHz, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>=1.75GHz, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>= 3.5GHz) is presented. The measurements of the prototype characteristics have shown that elevation angle of peak directivity of the antennas is oriented to zenith. Simulated S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> at stated frequencies with the following minimum values of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> = −34dB, f=1.85GHz; S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>=−21dB, f=3.7GHz; S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> = −22dB, f=1.75GHz; S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>=−19dB, f=3.5GHz are observed.

articleTitle: Nonredundant spherical near-field to far-field transformation for an offset mounted long antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: An effective probe compensated near-field - far-field (NF-FF) transformation with spherical scanning for an offset mounted long antenna, requiring a number of NF data that is minimum and equal to that needed in a centred configuration, is developed in this work, by applying the nonredundant sampling representations of the electromagnetic field and modelling the antenna under test (AUT) by a prolate ellipsoid. The interest for it arises from the fact that, for practical constraints, it could be not possible a centred mounting of the AUT on the scanning sphere centre and, for an offset mounting, the number of NF data required by the classical spherical NF-FF transformation can considerably grow due to the increase of the radius of the minimum sphere containing the AUT and centred on the scanning sphere centre.

Author Keywords: nonredundant sampling representations of electromagnetic fields

articleTitle: Improved localization by time of arrival for Internet of Things in 3D
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The demand of smart objects in our life promotes an advanced generation of communications under the umbrella of Internet of Things (IoT). In IoT, location-based service is one of the most promising services, where localization accuracy is a crucial problem. Rather than linearizing a nonlinear cost function used in ordinary localization problem, we propose a novel subspace algorithm by using the time of arrival (TOA) measurements. Our algorithm provides a closed-form solution and is validated to be robust for large measurement noise, as the dimension awareness and eigen structure of scalar product matrix are used. Moreover, we develop a Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CLB) for 3-dimensional (3D) localization by using the TOA measurements. We evaluate the proposed algorithm by comparing with CLB and show its performance through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of chaotic sequences for DSSS multiple access on software defined radio
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Paper presents an implementation of chaotic spread spectrum multiple access system model in LabView and USRP software defined radio. Chaotic sequences of different lengths are generated using families of one-dimensional maps and used for spreading in spread spectrum system. Performance of chaotic sequences generated using one-dimensional maps is evaluated against pseudorandom and orthogonal sequences.

articleTitle: Time-gating in antenna and microwave measurements using RDFT
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Due to the real-valued character of the measured impulse response, we propose the real discrete Fourier transform (RDFT) as a natural choice for time gating and removing reflections in antenna measurements. A computer program that applies the proposed algorithm was written. The program has a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) that allows easy visualization and comparison of time and frequency responses, as well as the proper choice of the time-gating window. The results of the software gating, applied on a measurement set-up consisted of two stacked patch antennas, are compared with the measurements in a reference chamber.

articleTitle: Broadband radiofrequency design of a laser diode bias circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Laser diodes are used in broadband communications including the radiofrequency range. Broadband design of a laser diode bias circuit is presented. The biasing circuit must have a high input impedance for radiofrequency signals, in order to prevent them from entering the DC power supply. The desired frequency bandwidth of the biasing circuit is up to 5 GHz. In this paper, two different biasing circuit designs are explored. Each design is simulated and optimized using electromagnetic simulation software. Based on the simulations, a series of printed circuit boards are designed and measured. It is shown that the power supply input impedance has a very small effect on the bias circuit input impedance value at high frequencies. Decreasing the resistor solder pad size and adding a slot in the ground plane achieves a significant increase in the input impedance value at high frequencies. It is shown that the new bias circuit design has a significantly higher differential impedance in the whole measurement bandwidth, and especially at high frequencies.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of UHF radiofrequency identification system signal for application in indoor positioning
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Location information has become very important by the rapid development of wireless communication systems. Specific areas where satellite positioning systems and positioning systems via mobile networks are unavailable, represent a major challenge in gathering information about the position. Most often there is a need for positioning within indoor areas, and one of the systems that can be used for positioning is RFID (Radio frequency identification). Usage of the existing of-the-shelf and certified products can significantly contribute lowering the system's cost. Prior to converting of-the-shelf RFID system into a positioning system, good understanding of system's signal propagation characteristics in indoor environment is mandatory. With this on mind, we investigated propagation characteristics of UHF RFID signal ranging from 865 to 868 MHz in simulated indoor environment using a passive RFID tag. The results show that signal used by the system may be exploited in obtaining the position of the tag.

articleTitle: Improvement of HF RFID detection for small and misaligned tag
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: A design of a reader antenna is proposed to optimize HF RFID range detection in parallel and perpendicular configuration. The reader antenna has a surface of 500 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the tag corresponds to 0.7% of the reader surface. For passive RFID system, if the reader antenna does not provide the threshold energy to the tag, this one will not be detected. This is the case of the misalignment systems with great difference size antenna. Another problem limiting RFID detection is the different possible tag orientations. In perpendicular configuration, the detection is weak, the tag can only be detected above the edges of the antenna. These limits are minimized in this work by using a multiple loop antenna including resonators. Electrical model is developed to calculate the equivalent mutual inductance of the system from the impedance matrix: the measured results confirm the simulated ones. The detection measurements validate the improvement.

articleTitle: A compact dual band implantable antenna based on split-ring resonators with meander line slots
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this paper, a dual band implantable split-ring microstrip antenna which operates at MICS (Medical Implant Services) and ISM (Industrial, Scientific, and Medical) bands is proposed for using biomedical telemetry applications. A miniaturized size of 9.5 mm × 9.5 mm × 1.27 mm is accomplished by using three split-ring resonators and meander lines slots on these resonators. There useful paths between resonators is used for optimization. Also, a shorting pin inserted between the patch and ground plane is used for the antenna miniaturization. The proposed split-ring implantable antenna presents 23.5% and 9.3% bandwidth, -48 dB and -24 dB maximum gains, 407 W/kg and 403 W/kg maximum 1-g averaged SAR values at the respective bands.. In this paper, only numerical results for the proposed design are presented.

articleTitle: System design to detect fall in elderly
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Fall in elderly individuals occurs due to anatomical and physiological changes induced by age and 30% of elderly face an accident of falling at least once every year. It is of utmost importance to provide medical attention immediately in these accidents. Seventy percent of these accidents end in mortality. The objective of the present study is to develop a system that would identify and report falling accidents in elderly. In this system, TI ez430-Chronos wearable watch would transfer patient information to Raspberry Pi via Bluetooth and Raspberry Pi would analyze the incoming accelerometer data and identify the fall, and then notify smartphones using Google cloud messaging. The designed system detects the fall and immediately notifies a relative.

articleTitle: Advanced data post-processing in modern antenna measurements
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Two useful approaches that allow noticeable reduction of the overall measurement time both in the far-field measurements and in the spherical near-field technique, while minimally compromising on the measurement accuracy, are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement of capacitive coupling to RG-213/U, RG-58A/U and twisted pair wires
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: This paper deals with coupling of electromagnetic fields to wire, namely capacitive coupling. First, it discusses skin effect and how the resistivity changes with frequency. The use of ferrite filters is explained in regard to interference suppression. Capacitive coupling clamp, a device used for measuring the coupled electromagnetic interference to the wire is explained, and its coupling to RG-213/U, RG-58A/U as well as twisted pair are measured.

articleTitle: Propagation effects on Satellite Communications and navigation systems
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The paper discusses the key propagation effects for satcom and satnav systems, the models used to predict them and some of the impairment mitigation techniques. For satellite navigation the ionosphere is posing challenges whereas for fixed satellite services the troposphere is the main concern. Mobile satcom services are affected by shadowing, blockage and multipath.

articleTitle: Calculation of the equivalente mutual impedance in complex HF RFID systems
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this work the improvement of HF RFID detection is obtained by the addition of small resonator in the reader coil. In conventional RFID system, the link between the reader and the tag coils is the mutual inductance, the added resonator is magnetically coupled with the reader coil, and then the link is expressed by the mutual impedance. Theoretical calculation of the equivalent mutual impedance of such system is reported and validated by comparison with HFSS simulation and measures.

articleTitle: Affect of magnetic field variation in ECR plasma discharge unit on polymer treatments
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Technology of argon plasma sputtering is presented, and a coil current (magnetic flux) variation effects on silicone based polymer surface has been tried to figure out. Silicone pieces were interacted with Ar plasma discharge under two different coil current values of 150A and 100A which produce fluxes of 87.5mTesla and 50mTesla at the centre of ECR discharge unit, respectively. The purpose of this research effort is to characterize and understand how coil current changes the surface capability of discharge unit while causing a change in ion-to-neutral ratio which is one the fundamental control parameters for processing efficiency. A requirement of the substrate not suffer any damage is also achieved. Polymer samples were exposed to discharge separately for different flux rate, and the results were monitored with SEM. Samples were kept through the treatment by 5 minutes after plasma initialization.

articleTitle: Performance investigation over 802.11ac communication environment
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: It is well known that the performance of wireless communication are quite sensitive to channel conditions and the transfer data rates are declining as the distance between the communicating peers is increased. In this paper are presented a set of results from a performance evaluation study of wireless communication based on the IEEE 802.11ac standard. The measurements were made between a pair of wireless access points interconnected in the bridge mode, located in close proximity, to provide the maximum performance. We have studied the performances of IEEE 802.11ac communication relative to Ethernet cable connections through traffic measurements, observing the necessary bandwidth and the packets response time for different sizes of packages generated over network. An important issue that was pursued was that the results to be valid and not influenced by hardware limitations. Therefore the processors load was continuously monitored, for both wireless devices and test computers.

articleTitle: Measurements of magnetic flux density in the vicinity of transformer station
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: According to ISO/IEC 17025 [1] standard the laboratory shall have quality control procedures for monitoring the validity of tests undertaken. Quality of test results can be controlled by participation in interlaboratory comparison programs. The firm Centar za mjerenja u okolišu d.o.o. has organized interlaboratory comparison of results obtained by measurements of magnetic fields in the vicinity of a compact concrete-housed transformer station located in Zagreb, Croatia.

articleTitle: Volume scattering from corn and wheat canopies at 32GHz
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The relationship between 32GHz backscatter measurements and wheat biomass and the underlying soil moisture content are investigated in this study. The received backscattered field deviates by about on the average of 2 dB between 0° and 20° of incident angle during a season. It is also represented that 00 responses is the most significant one as expected. The paper describes the experiment and investigates the radar sensitivity to biophysical parameters at different polarizations and incidence angle at different wheat phonological stages. Based on the experimental results, volumetric moisture content of soil contribution plays an important role in scattering phenomena and on radar cross section of canopies.

articleTitle: Metamaterial grid resonators structures for enhancing the radiofrequency magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The contribution presents a perspective approach to increasing the sensing coil's working range in magnetic resonance imaging using a planar resonant structures with distributed parameters. The working range increase consists in the improvement of homogeneity of the RF magnetic field generated by the coil. In the contribution, a novel resonant structure - Grid Quasi-Periodic Resonant structure, is introduced. Results of numerical modeling of the structure are presented. The results indicate significant improvement of the magnetic field homogeneity in selected area. In order to verify the simulation results, a test structure has been fabricated and it has undergone experimental measurement. The results of the measurement are in a good agreement to simulation results.

articleTitle: Hyperacuity in antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Hyperacuity of the human eye consists in the known capability to see very fine details far away from the limitations set by the number and size of its detectors. The authors of this paper have recently explained the hyperacuity of the human eye based on the use of the pupil diffraction before detection combined with a defined inverse problem. One of the most important concluding remarks of this study is the fact that, under some conditions, the inverse problem could be solved, meaning that some of the general rules used for designing imaging systems, including all the Synthetic Aperture Radar systems, could be reconsidered. Basically, if we are able to afford the inverse problem, we could assume some “blurring” in detecting samples, knowing that afterwards we would be able to restore the information, just by eliminating the known blur introduced at the detection process. In this case, we will try to apply this idea to improve radar applications. The angular resolution of a radar system is limited by the 3 dB beamwidth of the far field pattern. If we perform sampling at smaller angles, the obtained image will just be blurred by the radiation pattern of the system. Under certain conditions this blur could be removed by solving this inverse problem, and thereby restore a higher resolution image or signal. In this paper we will study the possibility to apply the concept of the visual hyperacuity to radar antenna systems, defining the conditions that these systems should satisfy, trying to find simpler and more robust designs.

articleTitle: Low-profile triband ISM dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile, low cost and easy to fabricate triple band ISM dipole antenna. The proposed antenna was designed to operate in the 434 MHz, 915 MHz and 2.45 GHz ISM bands. The antenna was fabricated with 20.7 × 2.7 × 0.15 (cm) dimensions and tested. The measurements show successful operation in the above-mentioned ISM bands and good performances for the antenna including -15 dB bandwidths, gain and omnidirectional radiation patterns. From measurements, this antenna also covers wireless applications within the 1.644 - 2.612 GHz frequency range including WLAN, Wi-Max and GSM.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental verification of a broadband amplifier in the Very-Ultra High Frequency regime
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this contribution we propose a numerical and experimental verification of a high power amplifier operating in the V-UHF (Very-Ultra High Frequency) regime. The designed amplifier has a push-pull configuration without negative feedback network in order to have low-distortion using high-level of AM (Amplitude Modulation). It is shown from the numerical and experimental results that the amplifier exhibits an output power of more than 100W CW (Continuous Waveform) and 200W PEP (Peak Envelope Power) over the entire frequency band from 30 to 512MHz. The amplifier can find application in military communication systems.

articleTitle: Inter-cell interference avoidance by active coordination of scheduling for downlink on LTE like systems
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this manuscript a new simple approach to inter-cell interference mitigation for the OFDMA based cellular networks is proposed, where the prolonged scheduling period and exchange of scheduling information among neighboring eNBs is used to reduce the interference among cells. Exchange of information could be carried over an interface similar to X2 that is standardized for the LTE systems. The process is described with the optimization by weighing the received scheduling information. The advantages of the proposed scheme are demonstrated by simulation results and compared to random resource allocation and soft frequency reuse.

articleTitle: Diffraction as a resolution enhancer: Visual hyperacuity simulation method
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Visual hyperacuity is the capability of the human eye to see beyond the acuity defined by the number and size of its photoreceptors. Optical imaging systems suffer from diffraction since light passes through an aperture and a lens system. Common diffraction-limited devices are designed to limit this effect and capture a sharp image. Nevertheless, the human eye produces a noteworthy diffraction effect which exceeds these limits, projecting a blurred image over the retina, where photoreceptors are located. On this basis, it seems difficult to understand it operating as a diffraction-limited system. Assuming that diffraction could be helpful to achieve visual hyperacuity, we present a method that intend to simulate and explain it: introducing a controlled diffraction, we are able to enhance the image resolution using post-processing techniques as interpolation and inverse filtering. Our approach uses diffraction to improve image resolution when captured with a reduced number of sensors, far from being a limiting factor.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of the planar resonators arrays for THz band
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The article presents results of numerical modelling of planar resonators arrays deigned for THz frequencies for various boundary conditions and material parameters. The presented results have shown the possibilities of using finite element analysis for THz frequencies and infrared band resonators arrays designing.

articleTitle: Some computational aspects of calculation of integrals arising within the framework of Method of Moments - application to bioelectromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Formulation involving the electric field integral equation (EFIE) and the related numerical solution via Method of Moments (MoM) variants requires tedious calculation of various double surface integrals arising from the use of vector triangular basis functions. The approach to evaluate such an integral strongly depends on the distance between source and observation points, respectively. In the case of a rather close interaction between the elements, due to a strong singularity, a purely numerical approach could fail resulting in the incorrect, spurious results. Hence, a combined analytical-numerical approach to extract the mentioned singularities is necessary. The present paper deals with an implementation of such an approach to the calculation of certain integrals types arising in the EFIE formulation for electromagnetic scattering from dielectric objects.

articleTitle: EFIE and MFIE for arbitrary sheets and closed form expression for the sum of fields on both sides of flat sheets
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: The most general vector form of the EFIE and the MFIE is given for arbitrary sheets. They are obtained through a complete and original derivation, taking into account the sharp edges that are always present in the case of sheets. These two integral formulations are then applied and particularized to dielectric and perfectly conducting sheets. It is also made clear when and how the tangential component of these formulations can or cannot be used to obtain the equivalent current densities in the framework of the Method of Moments. Finally, two closed form expressions for the sum of the fields on both sides of a flat perfectly conducting sheet are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Performance of textile logarithmic spiral antenna in on-body environment
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this paper we propose logarithmic spiral antenna which is manufactured by embroidering conductive yarn into common denim fabric. The antenna is suitable for integration with energy harvesting circuit. The original one-turn spiral was modified to obtain better coverage in the UHF frequency range. The free space antenna characteristics are compared with the ones measured for various scenarios when the antenna is put onto human body.

articleTitle: Improvement of wearable energy harvester conversion efficiency by improvement antenna-to-rectifier impedance matching
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: This paper presents an ADS simulation analysis of a simple energy harvester rectifier and an attempt to match the rectifier to a wideband antenna. The energy harvester is a voltage doubler circuit and the antenna has working frequency band from 0.3 to 6 GHz. It operates in the far field region, at low power input, which results in low conversion efficiency. Improvement of rectified output voltage is achieved by construction of Tchebyshev circuit that matches the antenna and voltage doubler in lower frequency band with higher number of sources from which the power could be collected.

articleTitle: Integrated microwave sensors in SiGe with antenna in package: From concepts to solutions
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In recent years wireless sensor systems operating in the microwave and mm-wave range became more and more popular. Automotive radar sensors are still the driving force for the development of higher integrated mm-wave sensors and thus pave the way also for applications in completely new areas. Industrial and life-science applications often require special functionality, smaller size, lower-power consumption, higher accuracy, easier applicability and more imaging capabilities, which leads towards flexible multi-channel multi-mode systems-on-chip (SoC) with antenna-in-package (AiP) solutions. This contribution treats some basic principles of radar and frontend concepts with respect to integration and indicates parallels and differences to typical communication radio chips. With advances in the packaging-technology the handling of mm-wave components becomes much easier, allowing new application areas. The embedded wafer level ball grid array (eWLB) packaging technology serves as basis for the additional integration of an antenna. Finally, realized systems of integrated SiGe-based sensors covering frequencies up to 240 GHz are shown. As application results measurements from a low-cost AiP based mm-wave imaging sensor at 160 GHz are presented.

articleTitle: On the connectivity of vehicular ad-hoc networks in highway scenarios
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: Modern vehicular technologies involve nowadays intelligent transport systems' (ITS) solutions, implying information technology, automation and communications. European Commission and transport organizations from worldwide are now focused on developing mobility as a service (MaaS), traffic safety, vehicular autonomy and environment protection. Vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANET), a specific subclass of mobile ad-hoc networks, has proven as an adequate support for a large number of safety-related mobile applications, such as: cooperative driving, cooperative collision warning/avoiding systems (CCWS/CCAS), environmental protection. However, some specific problems of these networks are caused by the large mobility of communicating nodes, which may lead to path interruptions or latency in transmitting emergency messages. This paper gives an evaluation of the connectivity on some case studies and presents possible solutions to cope with communication path disruptions on highways with low vehicle densities, addressing situations when not all vehicles are equipped with on-board units (OBUs).

articleTitle: Estimation of heavy-tailed clutter density using adaptive RBF network
publicationTitle: 2016 22nd International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics and Communications (ICECOM)
abstract: In this paper, a method for estimating clutter density using radial basis function (RBF) network is described. Clutter density is important parameter for data association techniques in single and multitarget scenarios. K-distribution is widely accepted model of heavy-tailed sea clutter, however, estimating its parameters using traditional method of moments (MM) or maximum likelihood (ML) approach require computationally intense task. Instead of this, a non-parametric approach is used (density is directly estimated, based on samples in validation volume of tracked target). During tracking process, returns from target and clutter are clustered using Linde, Buzo and Gray (LBG) algorithm, with fixed number of clusters and minimum distance criterion. Based on representative kernel of each cluster, density is constructed and integrated in Viterbi data association filter that also provides a track quality output. Since densities based under target-present and clutter-present hypothesis are available, corresponding likelihood ratios can be used to further discriminate target from clutter and thus enhance tracking process. Although the method for estimating clutter density is described using single target scenario, it is applicable to multitarget case e.g. using multihypothesis Viterbi filter.
